p: @workleap/create-schemas is a library for generating client code from OpenAPI Specifications.
If you've never used this library before, here’s the best place to start:

The src/codegen/types.ts file should be created.
During development, you can regenerate the types whenever your input file changes or configuration changes.
To enable watch mode, add the --watch flag to the CLI command or add watch: true to the configuration file.
If you have a more complex use case that isn't supported by @workleap/create-schemas you can try extending the behavior of the library by Creating a Plugin or using the JavaScript API.
If you think many users would benefit from a use case being officially supported, we encourage you to open an issue on Github.
Options passed to the CLI will always take precedence over options declared in the config file.
Path to the OpenAPI schema file

When running create-schemas from the command line, it will automatically try to resolve a config file named create-schemas.config.ts inside project root (other JS and TS extensions are also supported).

Project root directory used to resolve relative paths. Can be an absolute path, or a path relative to the current working directory.
Path to the OpenAPI schema file. Can be a local path or URL to a remote file.
Output directory path. The files that will be generated in this directory depends on the plugins being used.
Enable watch mode. Watch mode will regenerate the code whenever the input file or the configuration file changes.
Array of plugins to use. See Using Plugins for more details.
Options passed to OpenAPI TypeScript for type generation. You normally should not have to change them.
@workleap/create-schemas can be extended using plugins. Plugins can be used to ouput new files or modify files created by other plugins.
To use a plugin, you need to include it in the plugins array in the create-schemas.config.ts config file. For example:

The Plugin API is currently marked as unstable. It may change at any time.
If you desire a specific plugin, please open an issue on Github.
This work is inspired by Rollup plugin development.

A plugin is an object with a name and one or more build hooks, which follows our conventions. A plugin should export a function that can be called with plugin specific options and returns such an object.
Plugins allow you to customize @workleap/create-schemas behavior by, for example, modifying code before writing the files to disk.
The following plugin will add a comment at the top of every generated file.

To interact with the code generation process, a plugin may include "hooks". Hooks are function that are are called at various stages of the generation. Hooks can affect how a build is run, add a file to the output, or modify a build once complete.
The first hook that is called during the generation process. Use this to read the user configuration or emit new files.
Use this hook to modify a file generated by another plugin or to emit new files depending on the content of other files.
Run code at the end of the generation. This can be used to analyze the code that is being emitted.
The JavaScript API allows you to use the features of @workleap/create-schemas in any Node.js script.
Finds, loads, and validates user configurations. You can call this function many times and it will always return the latest user configuration.

This function converts all paths into fully qualified URLs, meaning a relative path like ./swagger.json will turn into file:///path/to/cwd/swagger.json. You will most likely have to use fileURLToPath from the node:url module or the URL class depending on how you plan to use the path.
